subject: Follow-up: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) competitive tests & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up & competitive notes from today's call — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)

Hi Alice / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary driver: strict patient-data residency and isolation for certain workloads; potential need for fully air-gapped inference for PHI-sensitive models.
- Current comparison set: Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem option) vs Hyperscaler managed endpoints (CloudCorp AI) and in-house self-hosting.
- Top concerns: network topology & connectivity, control-plane reachability, KMS/HSM integration, auditability (logs/SOC2 evidence), and onboarding effort.

High-level differentiators we covered: 
- Private control plane option (customer can keep control plane on VPC or run a self-contained on-prem package) — means optional zero-outbound mode for air-gapped POCs.
- Optimized inference runtime that supports quantized models and KV cache to reduce cost while maintaining latency SLOs.
- Clear rollback and rollout tooling for model pins and canary deploys (helps compliance-heavy teams).

Proposed next tests (we suggest running these in order):
1) Networking sanity check: confirm routing (VPN/Direct Connect), firewall rules, and ports required. I attached a short networking checklist and a high-level topology.
2) Control plane mode: validate Private control plane in 'connected' mode and then in 'offline/air-gapped' mode — confirm agent bootstrap approach and artifact transfer process.
3) KMS/HSM integration: test integrating customer KMS (bring-your-own) and key policies for model encryption at rest.
4) Audit & evidence: hand over SOC2 artifacts, logging retention tests, and sample audit logs export.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-comparison.pdf, networking-poc-checklist.xlsx (see attached).

Next steps / ask from Acme: 
- Can you confirm which internal engineers will drive the networking tests and a preferred week for the POC?
- Are there any additional compliance artifacts you need up front (we can surface SOC2 Type II, pen-test summaries, and specific control mappings)?

I'll loop in Camila (solutions engineering) to scope the POC checklist and Marcus (account lead) for commercial questions.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123


From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian O'Neill <brian.oneill@cloudcorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & competitive notes from today's call — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)

Vanessa,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Air-gap requirement — our security team's preference is to avoid any outbound connections from the inference cluster during normal ops. Bootstrapping via a secure offline media transfer is acceptable if the control plane can be run locally. Can Redwood provide an explicit workflow for the offline bootstrap & future patching?

2) KMS — we use KeyTrust HSM (on-prem). We need to know if Redwood supports HSM-backed keys and whether the control plane ever sees plaintext keys or wrapped keys only.

3) Timeline — we'd like to run a short POC in early December (target week of 2026-12-06) focused on networking and offline bootstrap. Is that doable?

I'm looping Brian (our cloud infra partner) to help scope the networking test.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
VP Product, AcmeHealth
alice@acmehealth.com


From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & competitive notes from today's call — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)

Hi Alice — thanks for the questions, quick answers and a draft POC plan below.

Short answers: 
- Offline bootstrap: yes — Redwood Private supports an "air-gapped" deployment mode. The typical flow is: pre-package runtime + model artifacts, transfer via secure media, run a local bootstrap utility that verifies signatures and installs the control-plane components locally. Patching can be handled via signed patch bundles that your infra team applies.
- KMS/HSM: we support external HSM integrations (PKCS#11 compatible) and do not require exporting plaintext keys to our control plane. We operate with wrapped keys and in some designs the HSM performs key operations locally. We can provide an architecture note specific to KeyTrust.
- SOC2 & evidence: we can share our SOC2 Type II report and control mappings; for the POC we can enable audit log exports and retention policies.

Draft POC scope (networking & air-gap):
- Week 0 (prep): exchange network IP ranges, confirm firewall rules, share topology.
- Week 1 (lab): setup connected Private control plane in your staging VPC, confirm workload routing and latency targets.
- Week 2 (air-gap test): run offline bootstrap using signed artifact bundle; validate KMS/HSM key wrapping and model loading; verify audit log export and retention.
- Deliverables: network checklist sign-off, POC runbook, audit log sample, and a short risk findings doc.

Attachments: poc-network-topology.png (high-level).

Question for Acme: can you confirm the staging host(s) we can use for the air-gap test and whether KeyTrust provides a PKCS#11 endpoint we can test against?

I'll start drafting the runbook and will include step-by-step commands for infra.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com


From: Brian O'Neill <brian.oneill@cloudcorp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & competitive notes from today's call — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)

Camila / team — good summary. A couple of items from infra security: 

- PKCS#11: KeyTrust exposes a PKCS#11 endpoint; we can stand up a test token for the POC. We expect Redwood to perform sign/verify operations without key material leaving the HSM.
- SOC2 artifacts: Acme will need the SOC2 Type II and the mappings to HIPAA controls (if you have a prebuilt mapping that would speed our review).
- Network ports: please confirm which outbound ports (if any) are needed for the connected mode and what exact firewall rules we must open for the initial bootstrap if we test connected first.

Also please confirm an estimate of how long the offline bootstrap takes (ballpark).

Cheers,
Brian O'Neill
Cloud Architect, CloudCorp (Acme infra partner)
+1 (617) 555-0145


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acmehealth.com>, Brian O'Neill <brian.oneill@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & competitive notes from today's call — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)

Thanks all — quick answers and proposed MAP (mutual action plan):

Answers: 
- Outbound ports: connected mode needs outbound to control-plane endpoints on TCP 443 (HTTPS) and an optional metrics endpoint on 9411; for the air-gapped mode, no outbound is required once artifacts are transferred. We'll provide a one-page firewall matrix.
- Offline bootstrap time: typical bootstrap (artifact verify + install) is ~20-45 minutes depending on model size; signed patch bundle apply is similar and we'll include checksums/signatures in the bundle.
- SOC2 / HIPAA mapping: Camila will attach SOC2 Type II and our HIPAA control mapping doc in the runbook.

Proposed mutual action plan & dates: 
- 2026-11-22: finalize POC runbook and exchange staging IP ranges (action: Acme infra / Brian).
- 2026-12-06 to 2026-12-10: POC week — week-long lab & air-gap test (actions: Redwood SEs + Acme infra).
- 2026-12-17: POC findings review and decision/go-forward recommendation (action: joint review).

Commercial note: Marcus will follow up on the POC SOW and any travel onboarding if an on-site session is requested.

Links & attachments: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-REDW-017; sharepoint POC folder: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/drive/airgap-poc-specs

Please reply +1 to confirm the 11/22 prep checkpoint and the target POC week.

Best,
